layer: heraldry and remaining burg data (coa of record 14 state, record 30 provinces, record 15 burgs; burg type/group/population vs gazetteer wording)
summary: Read every coat of arms: the kingdom (1), all 123 shires (records 30[1..123]) and all 505 burgs, plus every burg's type, group, population, walls/citadel/port flags against its gazetteer entry. HERALDRY: the history held no heraldry at all (no arms, badges or seals in the annals, books, appendices or houses.json; the houses of custody have no beasts), so all 629 coats were missing from the history. They are now written into a new Appendix J (kingdom blazon and meaning, all 123 shires blazoned with notes where the history supports one, the capital, the 15 cities of 20,000+, 6 seats/holy towns, and a summary of all 505 town arms by pattern), with an in-world origin in 4 new annals events: the custody's seal taken by the crown (III-0138a: the trellis azure/Or and mascle are read as the galleries and the slab over the vein; the fess is the crown's addition), the roll of arms made for the maoir's seals when the shires were drawn (V-0015a; this also explains the exotic beasts copied from a Residency book of arms, and the shield shapes: all 441 Dia-thìrich burgs and Dia-thìrich shires use FMG's 'wedged' shield, all 64 Tuathaich burgs and the 11 northern shires the 'heater', so the heater is the humans' district-seal shape), town arms copied on the first chronicle circuit (V-0080a), and the hawk granted to Cnoc bheag (V-0132a). Faith beasts compared with the arms: most mismatches are explained in Appendix J without map edits (Caol leathan's lions/wolves of the gate; Inis thais's masoned field = Clach 'stone'; the capital's ermine = Uallach's black-and-white floors; the Deer school, which never worshipped the stag, bears none; Ceann mhòr's wolf head = the old magistrate's device; Doire shean's falcons left unexplained on record). 2 conflicts fixed by map coa edits: the Hawk's seat shire gets a hawk (falcon), the Scorpion's seat shire gets a scorpion Or. 1 naming glitch fixed (2 island shires' fullName 'Siorrachd Siorrachd …'). BURG DATA: groups/populations and gazetteer wording mostly agree already (an earlier pass wrote 'a village in name but a town of twenty-seven thousand' etc.; all 'N thousand' figures match populations). 11 gazetteer edits: 1 group mismatch (Cnoc àrsaidh town called village), 1 city called a 'town', 1 overstated size (Doire bheag), 1 'largest in this part' for the island's largest town, 1 Lake burg not placed on its lake (Doire fhada on Loch chrom), 1 Hunting burg with no hunting, 6 River burgs with no river named. Groups, populations and types left unchanged. Agree: 494 burgs' wording; walls/citadel/port mentions agree with the flags in all cases checked (the flagged hits were references to neighbouring towns).

map_edits.why: Siorrachd Cnoc bheag is the seat of Creideamh an t-Seabhaig (Mòd, the Hungry Hawk; first house at Cnoc bheag, III-0062; the Hawk houses seat their own custodian in this shire, V-0131/V-0132). The shire's arms had no hawk; the white billet becomes a white hawk, granted at the Hawk houses' asking (new event V-0132a). FMG charge 'falcon' (3 colours), same tincture and position as the billet it replaces.

The western Seann Skell is the seat of Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe, where the creed was declared (II-0218, III-0120). Its shire arms had no charge and the Scorpion's sign (a yellow scorpion: Cnut, an Scairp Bhuidhe) appeared on no Scorpion shire or town. Adds a scorpion Or over all (new key 'charges'; the coa currently has none). Written into the history in new event V-0015a and Appendix J.
The name 'Siorrachd fhionn' already contains the form word, so the generated full name doubled it ('Siorrachd Siorrachd fhionn'). Every other shire's fullName is 'Siorrachd <name>'.
As for [122]: 'Siorrachd Siorrachd àrsaidh' doubles the form word.

event.title: The custody's seal on the king's letters
event.body: From the joining of the crown and the custody the king's letters are sealed with the vein-house's own seal: a trellis of gold on blue, which the custodians read as the galleries of the mountain, with a hollow lozenge over it for the slab laid on the first break. The crown adds a white band across the field and nothing else. From this time the seal is the arms of the kingdom.

event.title: The roll of arms
event.body: The council's clerks make Clàr nan Suaicheantas, a roll of arms, so that each maor can seal his court's letters. The kingdom's arms are cut again from the custody's old seal, and every shire is given arms of its own. Many of the charges are copied from a book of arms left at the Residency, and so lions, parrots and crocodiles appear on the seals of shires where no one has ever seen one. The Dia-thìrich shires take the pointed shield of the custody's seal. The Tuathaich shires keep the rounded shield of the humans' district seals. At Seann Skell in the west the Scorpion's house asks for its sign, and that shire's arms are the only ones on the roll to carry a scorpion.

event.title: The town arms copied
event.body: The clerks of the first chronicle circuit copy the seal of every town they visit into the roll of arms, and the roll comes to hold the arms of five hundred and five places. In the north most are copied from the humans' old town seals, since few Tuathaich will show the clerks their own.

event.title: A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag
event.body: The Hawk houses of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag ask the council to put a hawk on the shire's arms in place of the white billet the roll had given it. The council agrees, and the maor's seal is recut with a white hawk among its twelve crescents. It is the first change made to the roll at a faith's asking.
